# ggb-plugins
**English** | 简体中文

Turn a 2D math problem — given as text or an image — into an interactive GeoGebra file.
A host agent

(Codex or DeepSeek Harness) reads the problem and writes a native Algebra/CAS
program; this project

runs it locally, verifies every stated condition, exports the `.ggb`,
reloads it, and delivers the
file with a verification report and a screenshot.

Chinese and English are supported. The agent picks the working language from your preferences
and co

ntext, keeps the original problem text, and never invents answers: it analyses conditions
and builds
the construction only.
## Demo
Dragging C keeps ∠ACB at half of ∠AOB while the construction, dependencies and checks stay live.
## What you need
| Requirement | Why |
| Codex or DeepSeek Harness (DSH) | Interprets the problem and writes the native GeoGebra program |

| Node.js 22+ with pnpm 11 | Runs the local CLI and prepares dependencies |
| `curl` and `unzip` | D

ownload and unpack the pinned GeoGebra runtime |
| Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge | Drives the appl
et headless during verification |

No extra model API key is required. Installation needs network access; GeoGebra and the browser
are

not redistributed with the package. Building release packages additionally uses `zip`, `tar`,
and `n

redistributed with the package. Building release packages additionally uses `zip`, `tar`,
and `npm`.

The current release is v0.8.5.
It ships a Codex ZIP and the DSH npm bundle. The Codex package is not

yet in a public plugin
directory, but the Release ZIP is installable; see the
0.8.5 release notes.

- Codex: installation and upgrade guide, in Chinese.
- DSH: independent headless profile guide, in C

: installation and upgrade guide, in Chinese.

To browse the plugin from DSH, enable **Experimental plugins → Custom plugin markets**, then add
thi
s source under **Discover → Add index source**:

The two clients install independently and share one execution and verification pipeline. Both
guides

end with runtime preparation (`setup-plugin`, which also reports the browser it will use)
and a rea
diness check (`doctor`).
## Your first problem
Enable the plugin, start a new host session, and describe the problem. Images can be attached.

> Use GeoGebra to construct triangle ABC, mark the midpoint M of AB, and connect CM. Colour the
> me

dian red. Drag A to verify that the midpoint and median stay linked, save the file, and open
> the i

verify that the midpoint and median stay linked, save the file, and open
> the interactive preview.

Construction, reload, and every automated check run headless without intermediate windows. A
conditi

on that fails or cannot be verified blocks delivery instead of being skipped; failures keep
their di

agnostics so the next attempt can be corrected. If necessary conditions are missing or
ambiguous the

agent asks first, and when you do not give coordinates it explains the initial
configuration it cho

se. The Skill defines what the agent may
and may not decide on its own.
## What you get
A successful run writes one delivery directory:
| File | Purpose |

| `<title>.ggb` | Native GeoGebra file named after the problem; open, inspect, and keep editing |
|

`verification.json` | Per-condition results: construction, reload, and interaction samples |
| `prev

iew.png` | Screenshot of the delivered configuration |
| `request.json`, `manifest.json` | Archived
input and delivery manifest |

Reports state which checks ran and how far finite interaction samples reach; they never claim a
gene

ate which checks ran and how far finite interaction samples reach; they never claim a
general proof.

The delivery directory sits at `<outputDir>/<title>/delivery/`. `<title>` comes from the problem
and

also names the GGB file; a repeated title gets `-2`, `-3` instead of overwriting an earlier
deliver

lso names the GGB file; a repeated title gets `-2`, `-3` instead of overwriting an earlier
delivery.
## Interactive preview
The preview loads the same delivered GGB and supports applicable point dragging, parameter changes,
and zooming without writing back to the delivery. The preview process exits once the page loads; the
window keeps working, and running preview again reloads it. Use `--headless` for automated checks.
## Use the CLI directly
Hosts call this CLI for you, but other local tools can drive it too:

To change an existing GGB, declare `base` in the request: edit colours, line styles, filling, or
vis

ibility, add objects, or update independent values and coordinates. `inspect` lists objects,
current

values, and the digest the request must declare. Deleting, renaming, and view changes are
not suppo

rted. Request authoring is documented in the
capability contract, in Chinese.

## Repository map

- `src/` — CLI, execution, verification, and delivery pipeline.
- `viewer/` — the local page that ho

sts the GeoGebra applet.
- `skills/` — the shared Skill both hosts load.
- `codex/`, `dsh/` — host-s

pecific plugin assets, install guides, and acceptance records.
- `examples/`, `tests/` — runnable in

puts and regression tests.
- `scripts/` — dependency setup, packaging, and coverage tools.
- `docs/`

— requirements and design,
change record, and
cross-client validation records. Historical records a

re indexed in the
stage archive.
